html:
The Ngambri, also known as Kamberri, are an Aboriginal Australian group who claim to be the traditional owners of the area of today's Canberra. The name Canberra may come from their name.

Their claim is contested. The Canberra area lay close to the borders of several peoples, among them the Ngunnawal, Ngarigo, Gundungurra and Yuin, and records from the early settler years are thin. Settlers moved stock onto the Limestone Plains in the 1820s, long before the national capital was planned there.
